bullets.title: Applying International Clinical-Skills Standards
bullets.text: International healthcare systems use different equipment, terminology, documentation and competency processes. Safe adaptation requires orientation, supervised practice and confirmation of competence before independent performance.

bullets.title: Complex Aseptic Procedures and Clinical Devices
bullets.text: Complex procedures involving vascular access, urinary catheters, enteral tubes and advanced wounds carry significant risks. Nurses must assess indication, maintain asepsis, recognise complications and evaluate ongoing need.

bullets.title: Integrating Clinical Judgement with Procedural Care
bullets.text: A clinical procedure should never become a task performed in isolation. Nurses must decide whether it is safe to proceed, interpret findings, respond to changes and evaluate the outcome.

bullets.title: Simulation, Communication and Professional Documentation
bullets.text: Simulation allows nurses to practise procedures, emergencies and communication without exposing patients to avoidable risk. International practice also expects clear handover, objective records and culturally safe interaction.
